properties.Name: Principality of Moldavia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Moldavia, 1713-1768
properties.Note: Russian occupation during the Russo-Turkish War of 1768-1774; the principality, an Ottoman vassal, kept its prince and returned to Ottoman suzerainty at the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1774). Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Wallachia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Wallachia, 1741-1771
properties.Note: Russian occupation during the Russo-Turkish War of 1768-1774; the principality, an Ottoman vassal, returned to Ottoman suzerainty at the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1774). Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Moldavia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Moldavia, 1775-1790
properties.Note: Russian and Austrian occupation during the Russo-Turkish War of 1787-1792, ended by the Treaty of Jassy (1792); never Russian territory. Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Wallachia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Wallachia, 1775-1790
properties.Note: Austrian occupation during the Russo-Turkish War of 1787-1792, ended by the Treaty of Jassy (1792); never Russian territory. Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Moldavia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Moldavia, 1792-1806
properties.Note: Russian occupation during the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812; only Bessarabia, east of the Prut, became Russian at the Treaty of Bucharest (1812). Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Moldavia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Moldavia, 1814-1827
properties.Note: Moldavia west of the Prut stayed an Ottoman vassal after the Treaty of Bucharest (1812); only Bessarabia became Russian. Cliopatria draws it as "Bessarabia" in these two years (removed below). Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Wallachia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Wallachia, 1805-1806
properties.Note: Russian occupation during the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812; the principality stayed an Ottoman vassal at the Treaty of Bucharest (1812). Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Moldavia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Moldavia, 1814-1827
properties.Note: Russian occupation during and after the Russo-Turkish War of 1828-1829, until 1834 (Organic Statute); the principality stayed an Ottoman vassal under Russian protection. Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Wallachia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Wallachia, 1815-1827
properties.Note: Russian occupation during and after the Russo-Turkish War of 1828-1829, until 1834 (Organic Statute); the principality stayed an Ottoman vassal under Russian protection. Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Moldavia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Moldavia, 1840-1848
properties.Note: Russian occupations of 1848-1851 and 1853-1854, then Austrian until 1857; the principality was never Russian territory. Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Principality of Wallachia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Wallachia, 1834-1848
properties.Note: Russian occupations of 1848-1851 and 1853-1854, then Austrian until 1857; the principality was never Russian territory. Cliopatria leaves it out and draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Bessarabia
properties.Claim: Cliopatria's Bessarabia of 1812-1813 is Moldavia west of the Prut (the same outline as its Moldavia of 1814-1827), which is drawn as Moldavia above; Bessarabia itself is inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Romania), 1916-1916
properties.Note: The Kingdom of Romania fought on in Moldavia in 1917 and signed a separate peace in 1918 (Wallachia was occupied by the Central Powers); Cliopatria has no Romania in 1917-1918 and draws Moldavia inside the Russian Republic

properties.Name: Principality of Bulgaria
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Principality of Bulgaria, 1880-1884
properties.Note: Created by the treaties of San Stefano and Berlin (1878) under a Russian provisional administration until 1879; never Russian territory. Cliopatria draws it inside the Russian Empire

properties.Name: Ottoman Empire
properties.Claim: Eastern Rumelia and the rest of the Balkans that Cliopatria gives the Russian Empire after the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-1878; Russian troops left in 1879
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Russian Empire of 1877-1879 south of the Danube, within the Ottoman Empire of 1880

properties.Name: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
properties.Claim: Northern Dobruja, given to Romania by the Treaty of Berlin (1878)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Russian Empire of 1877-1879 within Romania of 1880

properties.Name: Ottoman Empire
properties.Claim: Adjara (Batumi), Ottoman until the Treaty of Berlin (1878); Cliopatria gives it to the Russian Empire from 1830
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Russian Empire of 1830 between the Choloki river (41.87°N) and 41.45°N, west of 42.55°E: roughly today's Adjara, to within about 20 km

properties.Name: Austria-Hungary
properties.Claim: Western Galicia around Kraków, which the Russian army never took (its front stopped at the Dunajec river, about 20.9°E)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Austria-Hungary of 1912-1914 within the Russian Empire of 1915, west of 20.9°E

properties.Name: Kingdom of Sweden
properties.Claim: Estonia and Ingria (Narva, Ivangorod), Swedish after the Livonian War (Truce of Plyussa, 1583)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sweden of 1588-1594 within the Tsardom of Russia of 1582-1587

properties.Name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
properties.Claim: Livonia, returned to Poland-Lithuania at the Truce of Yam-Zapolsky (1582)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth of 1588-1594 within the Tsardom of Russia of 1582-1587

properties.Name: Duchy of Courland
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Duchy of Courland, 1734-1771
properties.Note: A fief of the Polish crown until 1795, ruled by Anna Ivanovna from 1711 to 1730 under Russian influence but never Russian territory; Cliopatria draws it inside Russia from 1713 to 1733

properties.Name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
properties.Claim: Polish Livonia (Latgale, Daugavpils), Polish until the First Partition (1772)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth of 1734-1740 within Russia of 1713-1733

properties.Name: Afsharid Iran
properties.Claim: Gilan and Mazandaran (returned to Persia by the Treaty of Resht, 1732) and Baku and Derbent (Treaty of Ganja, 1735)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Afsharid Iran of 1738-1740 within the Russian Empire of 1734-1737

properties.Name: Emirate of Bukhara
properties.Claim: Samarkand and the Zarafshan valley, Bukharan until the Russian conquest of 1868
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Emirate of Bukhara of 1822-1863 within the Russian Empire of 1864-1867

properties.Name: Emirate of Bukhara
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Emirate of Bukhara, 1918-1918
properties.Note: A Russian protectorate from 1868 (and 1873) to 1920 that kept its emir; never annexed. Cliopatria draws it inside the Russian Empire until 1917

properties.Name: Khanate of Khiva
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Khanate of Khiva of 1918-1919, cut to the Khorezm oasis and the Amu Darya's left bank down to the Aral Sea, as the 1873 Treaty of Gandemian left it (traced by hand to within about 50 km)
properties.Note: A Russian protectorate from 1873 to 1920 that kept its khan; never annexed. Cliopatria draws it inside the Russian Empire until 1917

properties.Name: Russian Empire
properties.Claim: Turkmen lands not yet conquered: Krasnovodsk was founded in 1869, the Akhal oasis taken in 1881, Merv in 1884
properties.Outline: Natural Earth's Turkmenistan, without the Khanate of Khiva

properties.Name: Russian Empire
properties.Claim: Turkmen lands not yet conquered (the Akhal oasis was taken in 1881, Merv in 1884); Russia held the Caspian coast from Krasnovodsk (1869)
properties.Outline: Natural Earth's Turkmenistan east of 54.2°E, without the Khanate of Khiva

properties.Name: Russian Empire
properties.Claim: Tejen and the Merv oasis, taken in 1884, and Panjdeh (1885)
properties.Outline: Natural Earth's Turkmenistan east of 60°E, without the Khanate of Khiva

properties.Name: Russian Empire
properties.Claim: The Pamirs, divided between Russia, Afghanistan and China only by the Pamir agreement of 1895
properties.Outline: Natural Earth's Tajikistan east of 71°E and south of 39.4°N, without the Emirate of Bukhara

properties.Name: Russian Empire
properties.Claim: The Ili valley (Kulja), occupied by Russia in 1871 'in trust' for China while Yaqub Beg held the rest of Xinjiang; Cliopatria draws no state there
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Russian Empire of 1880-1884 beyond its border of 1885-1894

properties.Name: Qing Dynasty
properties.Claim: The Ili valley (Kulja), under Russian occupation until the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1881) handed it back to the Qing, who had retaken the rest of Xinjiang in 1877-1878
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Russian Empire of 1880-1884 beyond its border of 1885-1894

properties.Name: Qing Dynasty
properties.Claim: Manchuria, occupied by the Russian army after the Boxer Rebellion (1900) until the Russo-Japanese War; it stayed Qing territory. The Kwantung lease (Port Arthur) stays Russian
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Qing Dynasty of 1905-1910 within the Russian Empire of 1900-1904

properties.Name: Pahlavi Dynasty
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Pahlavi Dynasty, 1936-1941
properties.Note: Northern Iran was occupied by the Soviet Union from 1941 to 1946 (and the south by Britain) but stayed Iranian; Cliopatria draws the north inside the USSR

properties.Name: Republic of China
properties.Claim: Manchuria and the Liaodong peninsula: the Soviet army, there since August 1945, left in May 1946 (it kept a naval base at Port Arthur until 1955)
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Republic of China and Communist Party of China of 1948 within the USSR of 1946-1947. Land the Communists held is theirs, as the smaller realm

properties.Name: Republic of Uryankhay
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Republic of Uryankhay, 1912-1913
properties.Note: Uryankhay (Tuva), a Russian protectorate from 1914 and fought over in the Civil War, was not annexed; Cliopatria draws it inside Russia

properties.Name: Tuvan People's Republic
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Republic of Uryankhay, 1912-1913
properties.Note: A nominally independent Soviet satellite, like Mongolia, from 1921 until the USSR annexed it in October 1944; Cliopatria draws it inside the USSR

properties.Name: Allied-occupied Germany
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Federal Republic of Germany of 1950-1990 and German Democratic Republic of 1949-1990
properties.Note: Germany within its post-war borders, divided into American, British, French and Soviet zones of occupation until the two German states were founded in 1949; never part of the occupying countries. Cliopatria draws each zone inside its occupier

properties.Name: Federal Republic of Germany
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Federal Republic of Germany, 1950-1957
properties.Note: Founded in May 1949; Cliopatria draws West Germany inside the United States until 1949

properties.Name: Second Republic of Austria
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Second Republic of Austria, 1947-1991
properties.Note: Restored in April 1945 with its own government, under four-power occupation until 1955 like Japan; Cliopatria draws each zone inside its occupier until 1946

properties.Name: Korea
properties.Outline: Cliopatria's Republic of Korea and Democratic People's Republic of Korea of 1948
properties.Note: Korea after Japanese rule, divided at the 38th parallel into American and Soviet zones of occupation until the two Korean states were founded in 1948; never part of the occupying countries. Cliopatria draws each zone inside its occupier
